hero.titleA: A calmer way to care for the people
hero.lead: Hearth connects what is already in your parent's home, like a Ring doorbell, Alexa+ and simple home sensors, to give you daily peace of mind. No video, no intrusion, and your parent always in control.
hero.imageAlt: An older woman smiling in her living room while her family waves from a video call on the TV

benefits.title: Daily reassurance
benefits.body: A simple daily signal that your loved one is doing well.

benefits.title: Less coordination stress
benefits.body: Visits, errands and tasks organised in one place.

benefits.title: More meaningful connection
benefits.body: Send messages and short videos to your parent's Hearth screen.

benefits.title: Built for privacy
benefits.body: No video, ever. Your parent chooses what to share.

how.title: From an ordinary morning to a calm answer.
how.lead: Hearth reads the small signals a home already gives off and turns them into one status the whole family can trust.

steps.title: Connect what is already there
steps.body: A Ring doorbell, door and motion sensors through Home Assistant, and a check-in button on the parent's Hearth screen. Nothing new to wear.

steps.title: Hearth learns the routine
steps.body: After seven active days it knows what a usual morning looks like. Until then it says “not enough data” instead of guessing.

steps.title: The family gets one calm status
steps.body: A normal day, worth a look, or no signal yet. Always with how Hearth knows and one proportionate next step.

families.title: Less worry. Fewer group-chat threads.
families.lead: One place for the whole family to see how Mom is doing, who is visiting, and what needs doing.

items.title: Why Cards
items.body: When a morning is quieter than usual, you see what was observed, her usual pattern, and one sensible step, like a call.

items.title: Piggyback Planner
items.body: Visiting Saturday? Hearth suggests the errand that fits your trip. Nothing is assigned until someone says yes.

items.title: Moments
items.body: Send a short message or video to her Hearth screen and see when it was seen.

items.title: Ask Hearth
items.body: Type “How is Mom doing today?” and get a plain answer from Amazon Bedrock, limited to what she shares.

dial.title: Mom decides what you see.
dial.lead: She picks a level on her own screen. Family members cannot raise it, not even an admin. Try it.

items.title: I'm away
items.body: Visiting her sister? One tap, and nobody worries about a quiet house.

items.title: A delegate she trusts
items.body: She can name one person to change her level for her. Nobody else can.

items.title: A big, calm screen
items.body: Large buttons, readable type, messages from family, and an honest help button.

privacy.title: Privacy that is enforced, not just promised.
privacy.lead: Every answer, in the app, on Alexa+ or from Ask Hearth, is built on the server from the fields she allows. Then it is written down.
facts: No video, pictures or live view. From Ring, Hearth keeps only “motion at the door” and “a door opened”.
No facial recognition and no guessing who someone is.
Vehicles, deliveries and doorbell presses are ignored. A visitor is not her routine.
Every view and every change is written to the Trust Ledger she can read.
Simulated data is always labelled, everywhere it appears.
Hearth is not a medical device or an emergency service.

works.title: Works with what is already in the home.

items.name: Ring
items.body: Front-door motion and door sensors through the Ring Partner API. Signed webhooks, no video.

items.name: Alexa+
items.body: Ask “How is Mom?” by voice through Hearth's MCP connector. Live Alexa+ connection is still in testing.

items.name: Amazon Bedrock
items.body: Ask Hearth answers in plain words with Amazon Nova. It can read, never act.

items.name: Home Assistant
items.body: Door, motion and appliance sensors you may already have.

self.name: Self-hosted
self.note: AGPL-3.0, on your own server or a home computer

hosted.name: Hosted family plan
hosted.note: We will host it for you. No date has been set.

items.a: No. Hearth never asks for video, pictures or live view. It uses simple signals like “motion at the front door” or “the kitchen sensor moved”, with a time.

items.q: What if there is not enough data yet?
items.a: Hearth says “not enough data”. It needs seven active days in the last two weeks before it calls anything normal, and a silent sensor is shown as a data problem, not an emergency.

items.q: Is this a medical alert system?
items.a: No. Hearth is not a medical device or an emergency service. In an emergency, call your local emergency number.

items.q: Who can change what the family sees?
items.a: Only the parent, from their Hearth screen, or one delegate they name. Every change, including refused attempts, is written to the Trust Ledger.
Yes. Hearth is open source under AGPL-3.0, and runs on your own server or a home computer.
